[시놉시스]&#13;\n&#13;\n아름답고 평화로운 바닷속 왕국에는 여.en:
[Synopsis]

There were six mermaid princesses in a beautiful and peaceful underwater kingdom.
The youngest princess, the most beautiful of them all, turned fifteen and was able to see the world of land.
The little mermaid falls in love with the prince, a man of the land, and wants to become a man, so she goes to see the sea witch.
The witch asks for the mermaid's beautiful voice as a condition.
Moreover, it is said that if the love with the person you love is not fulfilled, it will become a bubble and disappear forever.
But the Little Mermaid decides to become human for love...
The Little Mermaid's beautiful and heartbreaking love story.. Can the Little Mermaid become happy?

[공연소개]&#13;\n&#13;\n한국이 만들고 세계가 극찬한 공연 N.en:
[Performance introduction]

NANTA, a performance created by Korea and highly praised by the world, since 1997

Nanta is a comical depiction of what happens in the kitchen, based on the rhythm of Samulnori, a traditional Korean melody. 
It is Korea's first non-verbal performance.
Kitchen utensils such as knives and cutting boards are sublimated into wonderful musical instruments, creating a spectacular performance, a surprise traditional wedding, and a performance with the audience. 
With dumpling stacking, traditional Korean dance and samgomu harmonizing with the melody, and drumming with a refreshing ending that will make your heart flutter, etc. 
'Nanta' is a powerful performance that can relieve stress in a fun way for people of all ages and genders, regardless of nationality.

[공연소개]\n\n2026년 매주 월요일,\n대학로 성균소극장에서 펼쳐지.en:
[Performance introduction]

Every Monday in 2026,
Held at Sungkyun Small Theater in Daehakro
Lee Cheol-jin’s story of Seungmu, “Only Seungmu”.


Seungmu (僧舞) is a work of art that represents Korean traditional dance and is a highly aesthetic dance that captures both the spirituality of Buddhist practice and human inner emotions. Jang Sam's delicate lines, controlled breathing and rhythm, and aesthetics of still movement create a world of vitality and deep thought that explodes in silence.

 
This stage is a Seungmu dance presented through an in-depth interpretation by Lee Cheol-jin, a dancer who continues the orthodox lineage that runs from Han Seong-jun, Han Young-sook, and Lee Ae-ju. Having walked a single path as a Buddhist monk for decades, he fully displays the philosophy of dance and the density of time on the stage. In each movement and breath, the accumulated traces of practice and the artist's skills are clearly revealed.

 
〈Only Seungmu〉, which is held as an open run, provides a special time for the audience to face their own inner self through the echo of movement that resonates in silence.

[Performance introduction]
‘Empty space, warmth left behind’

<Sad Play> is the story of an ordinary evening of a couple about to break up. 
There are no special events or dramatic twists. 
Just the words we always said... the place we always sat... the cup of tea we always drank. 
But in that ordinariness 
There are quietly piled up feelings in our hearts that we haven't yet spoken about. 

This play
'It makes me laugh and then makes me cry quietly... 
It's a story that makes you cry and then laugh again.

After the show, the first thing you'll probably do is...
‘It will remind you of the face of the person next to you right now.’ 

Attractiveness of the work> ‘A play that is sad but warm and quiet but remains long-lasting’

*Does not forcefully stimulate the tear glands.
*Stories that remind you of couples, lovers, and parents
*We touch your heart calmly and without exaggerated emotions.
*A play in which ‘silence’ lingers longer than dialogue
*Deep lingering effects whether seen alone or together

[Performance introduction] 

We invite you to ‘Umlaut Music Kids Classic’, a classical performance for your children!

<What is ‘Umlaut Music Kids Classic’? >
This is a classical performance for infants (preschoolers) and their families starting from the age of 0, when they are too young to go to a concert hall.
This is a performance where children can see, hear with their own ears, and feel with their bodies the vivid classical music played at the concert hall.

< My child experiences this! >
- Helps brain development by using various senses!
- Children improve concentration and become emotionally stable while listening to classical music!
- Your creativity and imagination grow as you experience various sounds!
- Have a great time immersing yourself in the music by following the rhythm and singing along to exciting children's songs and classical songs!

< What instruments do you experience? >
- Touch actual instruments such as violin, cello, and cello with the player and ask, ‘What does this sound like?’ There is time for children to make sounds themselves!

< Parents can enjoy it too! >
As children and parents experience music together, communication and bonding between family members will naturally deepen, right? This is a time when parents who are exhausted from raising children can also heal for a while with music.

<The most notable jazz vocalist of 2026 selected by the legendary Decca>

[시놉시스]\n\n01 Living Machines, Mechanical.en:
[Synopsis]

01 Living Machines, Mechanical Life
Living machines, mechanical life: Machines indulge in self-destructive mechanical pleasure through movements that can be repeated infinitely while in operation, and human mortality sometimes causes us to fall into the inhuman power of machines. It suggests the possibility of new life forms through the process where life forms and machines indulge and merge with each other.

02 The Intensity of Fusion
Mechanization of unstoppable impulse: The human brain and nerves have an instinctive impulse to survive, but the mechanical instinct is nothing more than simple repetition. When humans give up their nature and accept mechanical impulses,
It reminds us of the moment when metal and flesh become more deeply intertwined, and makes us imagine the possibility of a new life form being born between humans and non-living things.

03 The Mechanization of Irresistible Impulses
Violence of fusion: The moment when machines and living things collide, lusting after each other, iron and flesh, nerves and metal collide roughly. Sensation and insensibility, life and inanimateness mix together, and the possibility of a new existence arises.
This fusion is not a simple union, but a field of creation where neural explosion and mechanical pressure intersect.
At the moment when metal and skin share lustful friction, the boundary between humans and machines becomes blurred, and a new being called 'pseudo-life' exhales like a herald of birth.

04 The Birth of Artificial Life
Birth of similar life: We are aware of the new life forms or side effects that are born.
Will they live in harmony? Machines with a human scent and humans.
It suggests how we should live in the future.

[공연소개]\n이번 공연은 행진곡의 생동감에서 시작해 영화 음악의 감동으.en:
[Performance introduction]
This performance is a colorful stage that begins with the liveliness of the march and continues with the emotion of the movie music.

Opening the performance, First Suite for Band – Alfred Reed delightfully displays the rhythm and vitality of a wind ensemble with a work consisting of marches, rags, and gallops. The following song, Pearl Harbor, quietly depicts human emotions in the midst of war with its lyrical melody.

In the middle part, John Williams in Concert, which contains the musical world of John Williams, is played, presenting the charm of film music that is both grand and touching. Afterwards, Beauty and the Beast delivers a fairytale-like time to the audience with familiar melodies and a warm atmosphere.

Lastly, Moment for Morricone, a compilation of Ennio Morricone's famous songs, is played, ending the performance with a deep resonance.

[공연소개]\n\n클래식 기타리스트 신주헌\n\n창의적인 아이디어와 감성.en:
[Performance introduction]

Classical guitarist Shin Joo-heon

Classical guitarist Shin Joo-heon, who is praised by both the music industry and the public for his creative ideas and emotional interpretation of works, majored in classical guitar and graduated from the Department of Instrumental Music, College of Music, Seoul National University.

He was recognized for his skills by winning prizes at leading domestic and international guitar competitions, including 1st place at the Korean Music Competition, 1st place at the Overseas Dispatch Competition, 2nd place at the International Music Competition Vienna, 1st place at the France Music Competition Guitar, and 4th place at the Adelaide Guitar Festival. Based on this, he has been invited to perform on major stages such as with orchestras and performances at the Seoul Arts Center, and is continuing his active international activities by giving solo recitals and invited performances in Korea, Tokyo, Japan, and Taichung, Taiwan.

He has collaborated with Seongnam Philharmonic Orchestra, Hanyang University College of Music, and Seoul Haegeum Ensemble, and has been invited as a performer to various festivals and stages to communicate with audiences, including a concert with commentary by Geum Nan-sae, Hyundai Motor Company STAGE

In addition, he served as music director for the IBK Industrial Bank of Korea's Win Class VVIP Concert and as the music general artist for Dokdo LIVE hosted by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, engaging in activities encompassing planning and performance.

Not limited to classical music, he has also been active in a wide range of popular music and content stages, such as PLAY THE GUITAR, musical performances, Nexon game music concerts, and various album production sessions, establishing himself as a performer who crosses the boundary between classical and popular music.

Recently, he has attempted to harmonize Eastern and Western music by collaborating with a number of Korean traditional music players, including duo activities with haegeum player Noh Eun-ah, and is continuously expanding his musical spectrum.

Meanwhile, his music is widely loved by the general public and music lovers at home and abroad through broadcast appearances such as SBS Amazing Competition Star King, KBS Music Room, and KBS Korean Traditional Music Festival, as well as YouTube and SNS content media.

He is currently teaching at Seoul Arts High School, Gyeonggi Arts High School, and Yewon School, and served as a conductor and music director for guitar ensemble classes at the former Armed Forces Financial Management Corps. In addition, he is striving to nurture younger students by running Shin Joo-heon's guitar class, and was awarded the Korea Guitar Association's Outstanding Leader Award.

In addition, he received the Korea Best Brand Cultural Artist Award in recognition of his musical achievements and contribution to the field of culture and arts.

Continuing his various activities, he is currently attracting attention as a next-generation guitar player, captivating the hearts of audiences with his beautiful tone and technically sophisticated performance.

[공연소개]\n본 공연은 전통 가야금과 25현 가야금으로 아리랑, 산조,.en:
[Performance introduction]
This performance is an interpretive performance that combines Arirang, sanjo, folk songs, and popular melodies with the traditional gayageum and 25-string gayageum. It introduces the depth of traditional music and modern reinterpretation, and proposes an intimate musical experience that communicates with the audience in a salon space.

[PROGRAM]
* Two Arari 
This is a performance piece that newly arranged Jeongseon, Gangwon-do, Haeju, and Jindo Arirang into traditional gayageum and 25-string gayageum. It is a lyrical opening song that conveys the emotion of Korean folk songs through various gayageum tones.

* Kimjukparyu Gayageum Sanjo 
Kim Juk-pa is a master who established the flow of gayageum sanjo in the 20th century. Kimjukparyu Sanjo is a representative piece that shows the artistry and skills of the performer with its delicate Sigimsae, various playing techniques, and gradually faster beats.

* <A Million Roses> 
A Million Roses is widely known as Shim Soo-bong's song in Korea, but it began with the song <The Life of a Girl Given by Marinya>, which was released in Latvia in 1981. It contains a mythological story about the goddess of the earth and fate, Mara, suffering because she forgot to give happiness to her daughter. It was later rewritten into Russian and became widely known as a love song, and today's performance tells the story of how this melody traveled across borders.

* 25-string gayageum <Doraji Taryeong>
This is a performance piece that reinterprets the representative folk song of the Gangwon-Gyeonggi region, <Bolaji Taryeong>, using the wide vocal range and harmony of the 25-string gayageum.

* Memories engraved in my heart - <Cheommilmil> 
The theme song ‘Wolryang Representative Ah Jeoksim’ and ‘I’m Still Loving You’ from the movie <Cheommilmil> are played on two gayageums.

[공연소개]\n\n합창단 음악이있는마을은 ‘한국어의 아름다움을 합창으로.en:
[Performance introduction]

Village with Choir Music was founded in 1996 by the first director, Lee Kang-sook (who served as the first president of Korea National University of Arts), to develop and distribute Korean choral music in the spirit of ‘bringing the beauty of the Korean language to the choir and to the world’ and to grow into a world-class choir. Currently, there are about 60 active musicians and members, including 2nd director Kun-yong Lee (former president of Korea National University of Arts), planning director Seung-chan Hong (arts management, professor at Korea National University of Arts), music director Jun-cheol Hong (former professor at Daewoo, Sungkonghoe University), and conductor Hong-soo Kim (currently professor of conducting department at Korea National University of Arts). We are striving to widely disseminate Korean choral music through a total of 22 regular performances and various collaborative and joint performances, and we plan to present composer Kim Jun-beom's cantata ‘The Missing Case of Samsinhalmae’ and various original choral pieces through the 23rd regular concert.

[Performance introduction]
Two pianists who imprinted the concept of ‘star’ in the classical world.
Peter Jablonski and Jeongwon Kim.
Appearance and charisma reminiscent of idols at the time of debut, and matching
Two artists who have charted unrivaled trajectories in their respective paths with their talent and musical depth.
Do you remember your first duo performance at the Seoul Arts Center 15 years ago?
Since then, through continued musical exchanges and friendships, he is on his way to becoming a virtuoso.
The two of them have become more mature in their interpretations and can communicate with just their eyes,
We will tell you a musical conversation that goes beyond a simple collaboration and spans the ages.

Pianists Peter Jablonsky and Jeongwon Kim debuted as star icons of the classical music world representing the 1990s and 2000s, and are performers who have received both deep musicality and wide public love. In this duo recital, Beethoven's Symphony No. 9, one of the most beloved symphonies by the public, will be presented in a special version arranged for two pianos by the ‘piano magician’ Franz Liszt.
In addition, through a colorful and fantastic program created by two pianos and four hands, the delicate sensibilities and excellent chemistry of the two performers are highlighted, and a deep musical conversation that only artists who have walked through the same era can be shared on stage.

퇴직과 이별로 마음의 자리를 잃어버린 ‘민경’은 작은 시골마을로 내려와.en: ‘Min-kyung’, who has lost her place in her heart due to retirement and separation, comes down to a small rural village and begins to spend her time quietly taking pictures. One day, an old man enters her camera, which focuses on landscapes rather than people and distance rather than emotions. ‘Deokgu’, a Vietnam veteran suffering from dementia. After losing his granddaughter in a car accident, his memory is gradually fading. Although he suffers from dementia, he sits in front of his house every morning and waves to his dead granddaughter. At the moment of taking a picture, he looks at the camera with clearer eyes than anyone else. The record that started out as a coincidence gradually becomes ‘Min-kyung’s’ day, and the time spent learning the story of Deok-gu’s family and trying to hold on to Deok-gu’s losing memories soon becomes a time to caress and heal Min-kyung’s own wounds. People who are losing their memories and people who have lost their direction in life. Two people with different wounds regain their smiles through photos and begin to share their feelings little by little. And finally, Deok-gu enters Min-kyung’s heart and says the words that resonate the brightest. “Kim~chi!” Like that one photo, the time between the two becomes clear again.

[공연소개]\n달음의 두 번째 정규 앨범 〈Coexistence〉는 ‘함.en:
[Performance introduction]
Daleum’s second regular album, “Coexistence,” is a musical work that depicts the harmony and balance created by different beings under the theme of ‘living together.’
This performance is centered around the sound of coexistence created by two traditional string instruments, the gayageum and geomungo. The program begins with ‘Dasreum’ based on traditional modes and continues through ‘Tal’, ‘dot’, ‘The Waves’, ‘Cracking’, and ‘Alive’, showing a musical narrative where tradition and modernity intersect. Each song expresses everyday emotions, cracks, recovery, and the energy of life in various ways and is structured so that the audience can comfortably immerse themselves in it. Daleum's unique performance style, which maintains the depth of traditional music while adding a modern sensibility, will provide a new experience to the audience.

[Program]
1. Dasreum

2. Tal

3.dot

4. Dodry

5.The Waves

6. Poison and Antidote

7.In the deep

8. Cracking

9. Alive

[시놉시스]\n\n2001년 9월 4일 월요일 오전 7시 39분. 한 소.en:
[Synopsis]

Monday, September 4, 2001, 7:39 AM. The moment a girl takes her steps, time becomes undifferentiated and stops. The girl closes her eyes, sneezes, and floats in the air.
In that moment, a perfect rainbow at an angle of 42 degrees unfolds before your eyes. The seven-color panorama from red to purple is replaced with everyday objects such as trains, sheet music, jackets, and swimsuits, filling the stage. The seven notes of Doremi Fasolassido overlap to create a huge chord, but the girl who is the protagonist of that moment is unaware of this wonderful cosmic phenomenon.
Starting from a sneeze, time flows back and forth. People around me, friendship, dating, learning. The girl looks at the world by breaking it into small pieces, and reaches sadness and resentment within it.
So the girl sneezes, breathing and spitting out all of this with all her might.

[Performance introduction]
Opening the most beautiful history book written in the language of music on a spring road
-The confession of the soloist becomes the sound of the choir... A special journey that continues a great legacy -

Bach, Beethoven, Brahms...and Schubert and Schumann.
The music of virtuosos whose names alone make our hearts beat has arrived in Mokpo riding the warm spring breeze.
This performance is a special stage where the beautiful 'German art song' that someone had quietly sung alone blooms again with the delicate harmony created by the Mokpo City Choir.
As we walk through the romantic forest following guest conductor Hwang Ji-hee's friendly commentary, we reach the premiere song 'Mokpo Station', where the music embodies our waiting and excitement. 
At the 'starting point of excitement' rather than the final station, please experience the scenery of the train flying into the sky and the Archipelago Sea becoming a constellation through the chorus.

[공연소개]\n2023년 [문턱]의 시작을 알렸던 무대에 김단비밴드 래인.en:
[Performance introduction]
Danbi Kim's band Lane was on stage to announce the start of [Threshold] in 2023.
Since then, the three-year threshold has moved forward with a new breath, and Lane stands at the beginning again.

<New Beginning, Lane> is a starting point for refining their respective meanings for both [Threshold] and Kim Danbi Band Lane.

Based on the experience accumulated so far, [Threshold] further improves the completeness of the performance and expands the scope of the performance by embracing various arts centered on music.

Lane redefines the meaning of the team name from 'Rain', which symbolizes comfort, to 'Rain (來潾)', which symbolizes coming clarity.

Dreaming of a place where clear sound always flows (來潾) and the sound of people visiting (來人) never ceases (來人), this performance shares the excitement and anticipation of the beginning, a little fear, and yet a cheerful heartbeat through music.

Following Kim Dan-bi's in-depth commentary and witty and witty progress, the performance and story naturally continue, and the audience crosses the time of a new beginning while listening to the music.

<New beginning, Lane>.
Sound and people meet again when I stand in front of them for the first time.

[Program]

Prologue - Pinocchio the Tree Child

The fairy who granted a father's wish for a child: “If you prove that you are brave, truthful, and not selfish, you will become a real person someday!”

Chapter 1: The Village Market

In the peaceful market, a greedy count oppresses the villagers.

Chapter 2: Grandfather Returns Home

Pinocchio and his grandfather's first meeting.

Chapter 3: The Way to School

Pinocchio, different from ordinary children.

Chapter 4: Pinocchio's Lies

Pinocchio bravely jumps into a traveling troupe... His nose grows longer every time he tells a lie, but it returns to normal with just one word: ‘Truth’!

Chapter 5: Pinocchio’s Wrong Choice

Pinocchio, who didn’t listen to his father: “You must learn to choose between right and wrong. Your ‘heart’ will give you the answer.”

Chapter 6: Inside the Whale’s Belly...

Pinocchio learns of his father’s love. Tears well up in his eyes as he worries and feels sad for his father, who has been trapped inside the whale’s belly.

Epilogue - Pinocchio, a True Person Found Through His ‘Heart’

Something magical happened to Pinocchio after he found his ‘true heart’!!!

[공연소개]\n\n[사전행사 1] \n\n제32회 국내학술대회 <한국무용.en:
[Performance Introduction]

[Pre-event 1]

The 32nd Domestic Academic Conference <Records of 40 Years of the Korean Dance Festival and Discourse for the Future>

As a preliminary event for the 40th anniversary of the Korean Dance Festival, the domestic academic conference <Records of 40 Years of the Korean Dance Festival and Discourse for the Future> will be held. Co-hosted with the Korean Dance Research Society, an affiliate of the Korea Dance Association, this conference will feature research presentations that academically survey the trends and achievements of Korean creative dance accumulated by the Korean Dance Festival over the past 40 years, reinterpret its artistic value and significance for the times, and explore future directions and discourse. You can experience this forum for discourse where Korean creative dance meets academia on Friday, April 3, at 1:00 PM in the Multipurpose Hall of the House of Artists.

[Pre-event 2] <Charm Series - Streets of Seoul Dance Film>

Capturing the charm of Seoul through Korean dance. Korean dancers visit the streets and spaces of Seoul, where the past, present, and future coexist and whose beauty is recognized globally, to express them through dance. The ‘Charm Series - Seoul Street Dance Film,’ which is garnering attention as a preliminary event for the Korean Dance Festival, has so far recorded scenes where the city and dance meet by newly portraying the charm of Korean dance in various locations across Seoul, including Euljiro, Seosunra-gil, Cheonggyecheon, Jongmyo-saigil, Gwanghwamun-Taepyeong-ro, Sungkyunkwan-ro, Seochon-gil, Yeollin Songhyeon Green Plaza, Seoul Station, Haebangchon, and Nowon Gongneung Forest Path.

This dance film is set to make the 40th anniversary of the Korean Dance Festival even more special, featuring Park Cheol-sun, winner of the Special Jury Prize in the Small Theater category at the 39th Korean Dance Festival in 2025, performing at Godeok Waterfront Ecological Park, and Yang Ji-soo, who presented an impressive work in the Small Theater category, walking through Seodaemun Prison by dance. In addition, the "Best Click Award" will be presented to works that record high view counts to commend the choreographers for their hard work in creative activities, promote the public dissemination of their works, and ensure that this leads to meaningful achievements in future creative endeavors. Videos by Yang Ji-soo on April 6 (Mon) and Park Cheol-soon on April 7 (Tue) will be released on the "Korea Dance Association" YouTube channel at 7:30 PM, allowing you to experience the streets of Seoul through dance anytime, anywhere, without being restricted by location.

[Side Event] 40th Anniversary Archiving Exhibition <40 Years of the Korea Dance Festival: A Record of That Time>

To commemorate the 40th anniversary of the Korea Dance Festival, the side event archiving exhibition <40 Years of the Korea Dance Festival: A Record of That Time> will be held. This exhibition is designed to archive performance materials accumulated from the 1st to the 40th Korea Dance Festival, share the flow of change and records, and allow for a systematic examination of the lineage and discourse of Korean creative dance. Through various archival materials, you can discover how Korean creative dance has evolved and expanded over the 40-year history of the Korea Dance Festival.

This archiving exhibition, held in the lobby of the Arko Arts Theater Grand Hall, captures moments from the festival's 40-year history through photographs and videos, aiming to share the history and flow of Korean creative dance with the audience. The exhibition, <40 Years of the Korea Dance Festival: A Record of That Time>, is free to view at the Arko Arts Theater Grand Hall lobby from April 8 (Wed) to April 19 (Sun).

[Closing Invitational Performance 1] Kang Mi-ri Hal Dance Company - Thought

[Closing Invitational Performance 2] Dance us project Kim Hyun-sun - Strangers

[Awards Ceremony] 2026 40th Korea Dance Festival Awards Ceremony

Among the total of 20 works presented at <2026 40th Korea Dance Festival - The Path, Trajectory of the Body>, the Best Work Award, Excellent Work Award, General Audience Special Award, and Best Dance Performance Award will be selected in the Grand Hall category, while the Best Choreography Award, Excellent Choreography Award, and Judges' Special Award will be selected in the Small Hall category. In particular, this year we are able to honor the choreographers who have presented excellent choreography and works by presenting certificates of selection as “Dance Artist of the Year” to the eight individuals selected in the Grand Theater category, while also commending the hard work of the outstanding dancers.

[Synopsis]

[Opening Invitational Performance] The opening invitational performance begins with a stage by the Honorary Chairman of the Korea Dance Association and continues with meaningful projects involving the board of directors and works showcasing the current state of Korean creative dance.

The opening invitational performance of the Korea Dance Festival is comprised of excellent works by many artists who have united their hearts for the festival. First, <Sound of the Night> by Honorary Chairman Yoon Duk-kyung, who led the Korea Dance Association as chairman for over ten years, will be presented. <Sound of the Night> is a solo dance piece that premiered at the ‘1990 Contemporary Dance Artists Exhibition,’ featuring a piece composed by Hwang Byung-ki inspired by Ahn Jung-sik’s Oriental painting, 'Seongjaesugando (Sound in the Trees).' This is a work that expresses the intensely dense moments of resonance amplified amidst silence.

A special stage illuminating this year's Korea Dance Festival! <Dance, That Exhilaration> by the Korea Dance Festival 40th Anniversary Project Team will be presented. A work that can be enjoyed by people of all ages, <Dance, That Exhilaration> premiered in 1982 and seeks to achieve a new level of perfection created through the unity of the audience and the dancers. A symbiotic structure is formed through communication between the dancers, musicians, and audience within the piece. The work maximizes its impact through visual mise-en-scène direction, combining Samulnori with contemporary music, incorporating theatrical elements into Yeonhee (traditional Korean performance), and modernizing traditional costumes. For this <Dance, That Exhilaration> stage, ten dance artists, including Lim Hyun-sun, Lee Ae-hyun, and Kim Yong-chul, who are board members of the Korea Dance Association, have come together with a shared vision for this year's Korea Dance Festival. In celebration of the 40th anniversary of the Korea Dance Festival, a stage of another 'Shinmyung' (exhilaration) created collectively by artists of the Korea Dance Association is set to unfold. Finally, <Resonance and Mystery> by Jeon Su-hyeon of the Altimeets Dance Company, which won the Grand Prize in the Grand Theater category at the 39th Korea Dance Festival in 2025, will be performed. Choreographer Jeon Su-hyeon’s <Resonance and Mystery> tells the story of resonance and rebirth that transcend time in our language, music, and art. It presents the energy of group dances that seem to shake the earth, and resonance achieved through the deconstruction and recombination of Korean art. Through these three works, this opening invitational performance of the Korea Dance Festival offers a chance to encounter the history, present, and new resonances of Korean dance, delivering the profound emotion of dance to the audience.

[Main Performance] 2026 40th Korea Dance Festival <The Path, The Trajectory of the Body> A stage of new works presented by twenty choreographers!

The main performance of the Korea Dance Festival unfolds as a competition stage featuring works under the theme of <The Path, The Trajectory of the Body>. The Grand Theater section features new works by eight choreographers at the Arko Arts Theater Grand Hall, while the Small Theater section presents experimental and distinctive new works by twelve choreographers at the Cotton Hall of the Dongduk Women's University Performing Arts Center. Conducted in a competition format, the Korean Dance Festival has established itself as a dance arts festival that discovers the next generation of choreographers in the Korean dance world through the selection of top and outstanding works, expands the representative repertoire of Korean creative dance, and leads new artistic endeavors.

[Closing Invitational Performance and Awards Ceremony] The Closing Invitational Performance offers a chance to experience works that have accompanied the revival of Korean creative dance, as well as award-winning pieces with a fresh sensibility.

At the Closing Invitational Performance, you can experience <Yeom (Thought)> by the Kang Miri Hal Dance Company, which has continued its creative work from the 1980s to the present and led the revival of Korean creative dance in the Busan region. The work *Yeom* offers a profound interpretation of Seungmu and has been praised as "an experiment on the limits of Korean traditional dance, another experiment on overflowing, and an inevitable undertaking." Traversing the transformation and deconstruction of traditional dance to solidify the identity and standing of Korean creative dance, *Yeom* is set to further illuminate the stage of this closing invitational performance.

Following this, *Strangers* by Kim Hyun-sun of the Dance us project will be performed. This piece is the winner of the Excellence Award in the Grand Theater category at the 39th Korea Dance Festival in 2025. It portrays those who cannot blend in as strangers, conveying the message that since anyone can become a stranger, we must acknowledge these differences and coexist.

Finally, the awards ceremony will announce the winning works that graced the 40th Korea Dance Festival in 2026, *The Path, The Trajectory of the Body*. Out of a total of 20 works, the Best Production Award, Excellent Production Award, Audience Special Award, and Best Dance Performance Award will be selected in the Grand Theater category, while the Best Choreography Award, Excellent Choreography Award, and Jury Special Award will be selected in the Small Theater category. In addition, certificates of selection as ‘Dance Artist of the Year’ will be presented to the eight choreographers selected in the Grand Theater category, along with the Best Click Award, which can be considered the popularity award for the pre-event ‘Street of Seoul Dance Film.’ We ask for your continued interest.

Please join us for the 40th Korean Dance Festival 2026, <The Path, The Trajectory of the Body>, where the forty layers of time accumulated by Korean creative dance and new movements to be superimposed upon them will unfold.

[공연소개]\n\n수요일 오전, 클래식 음악과 함께 하는 마티네 콘서트..en:
[Concert Introduction]

A Matinee Concert with classical music on Wednesday mornings.

We look forward to four meetings in 2026. Meeting between seasons—in April and May, and September and October—we begin a conversation with music.

Author Kim Young-ha joins this series. Each month, he presents new stories and a curation of music personally selected by the author.

The Reason for Music, The Reason for Travel

Walking through a novelist's eyes and remembering Europe by the melodies of music

Why do we travel?

Bestselling author and storyteller of our time, Kim Young-ha, serves as the host of the 2026 Matinee Series, inviting the audience to the romantic cities of Europe.

This series is a high-quality lecture concert that weaves together classical music with the unfamiliar landscapes and people the author encountered while traveling through Italy, Germany, France, and Spain, as well as the humanistic insights he drew from them. It vividly brings the brilliant sunlight, solitary contemplation, and artistic inspiration felt during travels onto the stage.

During the leisurely morning hours, *The Musical*—a blend of author Kim Young-ha’s charming storytelling and music filled with local atmosphere—will be a special break that will reawaken the "reason for travel" for those weary from their repetitive daily lives.

Life is Like a Festival, the Land of Opera

In warm April, Italians live every day like the protagonists on a stage. They eat well, laugh heartily, and love passionately. Join author Kim Young-ha as he shares the cheerful and optimistic lifestyle of Italians. It is the most exciting stage to fill you with the vitality of spring while enjoying splendid and dramatic opera arias and romantic Italian art songs.

경기도 시흥시 경기과기대로 284에 위치한 시흥에코센터 초록배곧은 자연·.en:
Located at 284 Gyeonggi Institute of Technology-daero, Siheung-si, Gyeonggi-do, the Siheung Eco Center Green Baegot is a complex educational space filled with exhibitions and hands-on experiences themed around nature and the environment.

Since its completion in 2015 and opening in 2016, it has established itself as an eco-friendly space frequently visited by families.

1st Floor: Composed of a permanent exhibition hall, a special exhibition hall, and a children's experience exhibition room, visitors can easily and enjoyably experience various environmental themes.

2nd Floor: Spaces for education and discussion, such as an environmental education room, group discussion rooms, and a multi-purpose room, are provided.

Outdoors: Various ecological experiences and play activities have been created, including an ecological pond, an ecological vegetable garden, a nature playground, and an electric vehicle experience area, allowing visitors to freely use both indoor and outdoor spaces.

Diverse Environmental Exhibitions: Exhibitions and educational programs featuring themes that change annually, such as resource recycling and climate change, are conducted, allowing visitors to learn various ways to protect nature.

Hands-on Activities: Activities linked to real life are available, such as a unique game of listening to the sounds of the forest with paper tubes, eco-friendly lifestyle experiences like rainwater piggy banks, and an ice pack recycling campaign. Ecological Learning in Outdoor and Rooftop Spaces: You can observe and experience plants and insects firsthand at the ecological pond and vegetable garden.

Electric Vehicle Experience Zone for Children: Operated on weekends and seasonally, this zone features traffic lights and roads, offering a fun driving experience (Ages 6–10, Admission Fee applies). Permanent Exhibition Hall: Toddlers~Elementary Students 1,000 won / Middle, High School Students & Soldiers 1,500 won / Adults 2,000 won

Outdoor Electric Cars (Ages 6~10): 500 won

4D Theater: Toddlers~Elementary Students 1,000 won / Middle, High School Students & Soldiers 1,000 won / Adults 2,000 won

50% discount for Siheung citizens

Free admission for toddlers aged 4 and under

Closed: Every Monday, January 1st, Lunar New Year & Chuseok holidays

No pets allowed

No food or drinks allowed

Free parking available; no reservation required

This is a place where you can learn about environmental protection and various eco-friendly materials in a fun way while completing missions such as Seed Cards and Stamp Tours.

It takes about 1 hour to view the entire site.

The outdoor electric car experience is available only for ages 6 to 10. While the 4D videos are educational and entertaining, children under the age of 5 may find them frightening due to the moving chairs and gentle wind and water sprays. Since 4D screening times are fixed, we recommend checking the schedule in advance before visiting.

The exhibits and hands-on activities may be slightly challenging for infants and toddlers aged 5 and under.

Various free hands-on programs and exhibitions are available, so we recommend checking the official website before your visit.

Both indoor exhibits and outdoor activities are available, allowing children to naturally learn about and enjoy the environment.

As an environmental education venue where exhibitions, hands-on activities, and play come together, it is an ideal space for those looking to spend meaningful time with their families.

1F: International Exhibition Hall, Life Gallery, Handok History Room, Jeseok Hall

Korea Pavilion: You can explore the history of traditional Korean medicine, cultural heritage (6 National Treasures, 2 City/Provincial Designated Cultural Properties), various medical texts, and the appearance of an old Korean traditional medicine clinic.

International Pavilion: The history of medicine from both the East and West, including Germany, the UK, the US, China, and Japan, is displayed together. A 19th-century German pharmacy and Dr. Fleming's laboratory have also been recreated.

Handok Archives: Introduces Handok's corporate history and growth process through various materials.

Jeseok Hall: Items donated by the founder, Honorary Chairman Kim Shin-kwon, are on display.

Life Gallery: You can appreciate contemporary art and artworks themed around life.

Operating Hours: 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM

Closed: Every Monday

The medical library within the museum houses approximately 9,000 medical books.

Next to the museum is the Factory Tour Center, which features a greenhouse café atmosphere, making it a great place to take a break.

While you can tour the exhibition halls without a reservation, the hands-on programs are well-organized, so we recommend booking in advance to participate. The experience schedule is available on the website, so you can select the experience and time slot you prefer.

Be sure to stop by the glass greenhouse cafe (Factory Tour Center) in front of the parking lot, where you can experience packaging medicine yourself.

Picnic sets are also available for rent, so if the weather is nice, enjoy a picnic as well.

Bring your earphones and view the exhibition while listening to the commentary.

There are tourist attractions nearby, such as the Factory Tour Center, the Ban Ki-moon Peace Memorial Hall, and the Korea Craft Brewery, so it is recommended to visit them as well.

Composed of two floors, each floor and exhibition room covers a variety of themes, including the history of Wando, the marine environment, and marine life.

The first floor features a lobby, a special exhibition room, and an experience room, allowing for hands-on activities.

The Ecology Room on the second floor features a trick art photo zone, making it a great spot for taking photos.

The interior of the exhibition hall is equipped with colorful cushions and sofas, as well as various interactive content, to engage children.

It is filled with diverse hands-on elements that children can participate in, such as a large digital aquarium, puzzles, rubbings, fishing, and abalone farming.

Visitors can observe and learn about the diverse ecosystems of Wando's sea and marine life (microalgae, large seaweed, crustaceans, shellfish, fish, etc.) up close.

Visitors can naturally learn about the importance of the ocean and seaweed, as well as how to protect marine ecosystems.

Educational exhibits are prepared to encourage visitors to ask questions and think for themselves regarding environmental issues, such as marine pollution and the future of the ocean. With plenty of hands-on activities and experience corners, such as puzzle solving and rubbings, children will never get bored.

It is situated approximately a 2-3 minute walk from Exit 4 of Jamsil Station, offering excellent accessibility via public transportation.

Three hours of free parking are provided when using the Lotte World Mall underground parking lot, and all-day pass holders can receive a free parking voucher for six hours.

Approximately 100 diverse career booths are available, allowing children to directly experience various professions they have always dreamed of, such as firefighters, police officers, flight attendants, doctors, and scientists.

In front of each experience booth, information regarding the duration, capacity, appropriate age, and the dedicated currency (Kidzo) earned or spent through the experience is clearly displayed.

Upon entry, each child receives a traveler's check worth 50 Kidzo, which is earned or spent through booth experiences.

Kidzo can be used to purchase actual goods, such as toys and stationery, at the department store within KidZania.

The interior is well-equipped with safety and amenities for children, and services for family visitors, such as stroller rentals and nursing rooms, are also available.

Located in the central plaza on the second floor, the KidZateria (cafeteria) allows visitors to comfortably enjoy a variety of children's favorite dishes, such as omurice, pork cutlets, and fried chicken.

Children can actively choose and experience different professions firsthand, which greatly aids in career exploration, leadership development, and social skills.

Parental satisfaction is also high as parents are given free time to rest while their children participate in activities. It offers excellent accessibility to downtown Seoul and the subway, and is also convenient for visiting in conjunction with nearby tourist attractions such as Lotte World.

Located at 69, Sanroknam-ro 762beon-gil, Andeok-myeon, Seogwipo-si, Jeju, the Bontae Museum is a special space designed to harmonize with Jeju's beautiful nature.

"Bontae" means "original form," and the museum was established in 2012 to explore the inherent beauty of humanity through traditional and modern art.

Designed by world-renowned architect Tadao Ando, ​​it boasts a unique and sensuous architectural beauty where exposed concrete, light, and water blend together.

Based on the overarching themes of the meeting of nature and architecture, tradition and modernity, and the world and Korea, the museum operates various exhibitions, hands-on experiences, and educational programs.

The Bontae Museum consists of five exhibition halls.

Hall 1 – Traditional Crafts Hall
Various traditional lifestyle crafts, such as Korean small tables (soban), wooden furniture, bojagi (wrapping cloths), and pillows, are on display, allowing visitors to experience our ancient lifestyle culture and the beauty of artisans.

Hall 2 – Contemporary Art Museum
Contemporary art works by world-famous artists such as Picasso, Dali, Andy Warhol, and Nam June Paik are exhibited here. You can explore the trends of global art with your child.

Gallery 3 – Yayoi Kusama Special Hall
Representative works by Japanese contemporary art master Yayoi Kusama, such as "Pumpkin" and "Infinity Mirror Room," are on display, allowing children to have a fascinating art experience.

Gallery 4 – Traditional Funeral Hall
Crafts related to the funeral customs of the past, such as funeral biers and wooden figures, are exhibited here, making it easy and interesting to learn about our traditional culture.

Gallery 5 – Special Exhibition Hall
Special exhibitions with various themes are held depending on the season, so it is a good idea to check the exhibition information before visiting.

In addition to the indoor areas, there are various sculptures and beautiful walking paths outdoors, allowing families to walk together and experience both art and nature simultaneously.

Visiting the museum itself becomes an experience where you can view various artworks up close, fostering creativity and sensibility in children.

There are corners prepared where children can enter and experience unique spaces, such as Yayoi Kusama's "Infinity Mirror Room," making art a fun and engaging experience. At the Traditional Crafts Hall, you can naturally learn about our culture through familiar everyday objects, making it an educational experience.

Operating Hours: Daily 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM

Duration of Visit: Approximately 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours

Admission is free for infants under 36 months (proof of age required)

There is ample outdoor space, so we recommend a family stroll after viewing the exhibition.

It is located about 40 minutes by car from Jeju International Airport and about 15 minutes from the Jeju International Convention Center.

If using public transportation, it takes about 1 hour to 1 hour 20 minutes via bus and transfers.

Amenities Available: Diaper changing station, stroller rental, parking, reservations

Amenities Not Available: High chairs, nursing room

There are many stairs inside the museum, so moving around with a stroller may be difficult.

Admission is free for children under 36 months.

Located at 1268 Jungmisan-ro, Okcheon-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, Jungmisan Observatory is situated within the Jungmisan Natural Recreation Forest at an elevation of approximately 420m to 437m.

It boasts excellent accessibility, being only about an hour's drive from Seoul, and is considered one of the top spots near the metropolitan area for observing a wide variety of stars due to its low pollution levels.

Astronomical Observation Programs: Visitors can directly observe stars, planets, the moon, and seasonal constellations using multiple telescopes.

Educational and Video Programs: Video education and simulation programs designed to easily convey basic space science knowledge are available to stimulate children's curiosity.

Hands-on Activities: Visitors can experience "touching" the universe firsthand through expert explanations and hands-on practice.

Since this is a reservation-only program, you must make a reservation via the official website or a booking platform before your visit.

Entry is permitted approximately one hour before the program starts; it is recommended to arrive at least 10 minutes before your scheduled time.

Driving may be difficult in the dark surroundings, so we recommend arriving early to ensure safe transportation.

옥토끼우주센터는 인천 강화도에 위치한 국내 최초의 우주 과학 테마파크입니.en:
Okto-tokki Space Center is Korea's first space science theme park, located on Ganghwa Island in Incheon. As a complex cultural space combining space, science, art, exploration, and play, it is an experiential travel destination designed to stimulate children's curiosity and creativity.

The indoor exhibits and activities are recommended for children who are interested in robots, space, and science, or for slightly older children.

The indoor space, spanning approximately 2,000 pyeong (about 6,600 square meters), displays around 500 actual space exhibits.

With exhibition halls featuring various themes such as the history of space development, the birth of rockets and spacecraft, the lives of astronauts, and exploration of Mars and the Moon, visitors can easily learn about and experience space with their children.

Vivid videos on the themes of space and science can be viewed in the 3D cinema.

Taking commemorative photos dressed as if wearing a spacesuit and riding six types of space experience rides are also very popular activities.

On a vast outdoor site spanning approximately 16,000 pyeong (about 53,000 square meters), a Dinosaur Forest has been created where large, moving dinosaurs come to life. Approximately 40 to 63 large dinosaur models are on display, offering an experience that feels like time travel to the dinosaur era.

There are various themed play areas, including a Robot Park, Water Cannon Park, Logos Garden, and a spacious observation tower.

The Four Seasons Sledding Park offers diverse sledding experiences (snow sledding, rubber sledding) depending on the season; it transforms into a water playground in the summer and a boating area in spring and autumn, allowing visitors to enjoy a variety of activities throughout the year.

A mini-train, boat rides, and a spacious landscaped area for outdoor play are also available.

Amenities provided: Nursing room, diaper changing station, stroller rental, parking, reservations

Amenities not provided: High chairs

Discounts are available when booking via Naver.

Parking Lot 1 is closest to the entrance. Address: 403, Ganghwadong-ro, Buleun-myeon, Ganghwa-gun, Incheon

14 Galleries, Over 1,000 Interactive Exhibitions

Each gallery, themed around various subjects, is filled with exhibits that allow visitors to touch, experiment with, and experience firsthand. Children can naturally learn scientific principles through themes such as "Optical Illusions," "Mirror Mazes," and "Earth and the Environment."

Special Exhibitions and Unique Experiences

Various special exhibitions are available, covering emotions, psychology, and the mysteries of nature, such as "Phobias – The Science of Fear." Additionally, daily events are held, including experimental demonstrations like the "Fire Tornado Show," "Giant Cockroach Observation," and "Star Observation at the Observatory."

KidsSTOP

A space where children aged 8 and under can learn science and technology through play, designed with hands-on experiences that young children can safely enjoy.

Omni-Theatre

Singapore's only dome-shaped IMAX theater, where visitors can enjoy science documentaries and nature videos on a grand scale. Snow City

This is an indoor space where you can enjoy sub-zero snow and experience winter activities such as sledding and snowman building.

If you visit the Science Centre, you can use the outdoor water park for free. If you plan to use the water park, please bring a swimsuit, a change of clothes, and drinking water.

Weather Play Experience Hall (1st Floor): You can learn about the basic elements that make up weather, such as wind, sun, and water, through various interactive exhibits and games.

Marine Weather Phenomena Hall (2nd Floor): You can realistically experience weather phenomena occurring at sea, such as typhoons, tsunamis, waves, and tornadoes.

Marine Weather Observation Hall: You can learn about the principles and various measuring instruments used to observe ocean weather.

Marine Climate Change Hall: You can enjoy exhibitions and interactive experiences themed around the changing ocean, climate, and future environment.

Media Art Hall: You can sit comfortably and appreciate the art while listening to the sound of rain falling, and you can also participate in a live sketching experience where you draw on sea animal templates and have them displayed on the screen.

Since it is an indoor exhibition hall, you can visit without worry even on rainy days.

There are many things to see and experience, so we recommend visiting with ample time.

Tickets can be purchased at the kiosk inside the entrance, and those eligible for free admission can pick up their tickets at the information desk. Located in a standalone building next to the Hoecheon 4-dong Administrative Welfare Center public parking lot, the first floor houses an electric vehicle charging station, while the experience space is on the second floor.

Through large displays and immersive media, visitors can easily check data on fine dust, wind patterns, and environmental conditions in Yangju City.

By directly touching the screen, visitors can experience various atmospheric information and simulations, such as wind pattern analysis and fine dust analysis.

Utilizing 'HoloLens 2' for holographic AR (augmented reality) experiences, visitors can perform environmental missions by manipulating virtual objects appearing before their eyes with their hands.

Through virtual reality experiences such as the Metaverse and Metahuman, visitors can directly experience Yangju City's environmental protection activities and urban transformation.

Programs that allow children to create and learn firsthand, such as DIY experience kits, are also offered to foster their curiosity and creativity.

Due to the physical requirements for wearing the equipment, XR experiences are recommended for children aged 8 and older, while Metaverse virtual experiences are recommended for younger children.

Environmental education and experiential activities for various age groups are regularly conducted in the education room. Individual visitors can freely visit at any time and enjoy free experiences ranging from Metaverse virtual exhibitions to Hologram AR and XR.

As the only municipal astronomical science museum in Northern Gyeonggi Province, it is a special space where you can experience stars and the universe up close with your children.

Located within Pocheon Art Valley, you can enjoy science experiences amidst a magnificent landscape where nature and art harmonize.

Anyone can touch and interact with fascinating and fun exhibits, and cultivate scientific creativity through hands-on programs.

1st Floor: Lobby, Information Desk, Nursing Room, Exhibition Hall 1

2nd Floor: Exhibition Halls 2 & 3, Lounge, Restrooms

3rd Floor: Planetarium (Constellation explanations, 4D special video viewing, etc.)

Rooftop: Astronomical Observatory (Equipped with the nation's highest-quality telescopes; observation of the Sun, Moon, and planets is possible)

The exhibition halls are open for free viewing, while observation and planetarium programs operate on a same-day on-site registration basis.

Admission is free with the entry of Pocheon Art Valley.

Viewing the exhibition halls alone is substantial enough, so I highly recommend visiting even if you do not participate in any programs. The planetarium program is very popular, so wait times may be long on weekends.

At the planetarium, you can enjoy constellation stories and special videos every hour, stimulating children's curiosity.

Please note that the 4D video screening involves vibrations, so children who are easily frightened should take note.

You can experience observing the sun during the day and the moon and planets at night.

It is faster to go to the Astronomical Science Hall first after getting off the monorail, get on the planetarium standby, and then explore other areas. Monorail operations are temporarily suspended until November 30, 2023.

You can enjoy the experience more if you research your child's constellation beforehand.

Various educational programs, such as weekend science experience classes and science lectures, are offered, making it suitable for family visits.

While anyone can view the exhibition halls regardless of height or age, participation in the celestial observation and projection programs is limited to children aged 5 and older who are at least 100cm tall.

There is a nursing room on the first floor; if needed, please ask at the information desk to use it. Tickets are distributed free of charge on the day of admission at the information desk on the 1st floor (up to 4 tickets per person); online reservations are not available.

You can learn through your five senses by seeing and touching fascinating models of the universe, stars, and planets firsthand.

1st Floor: Aviation Hall

This section consists of exhibits on the history and principles of airplanes, displays of various aircraft models, and a space where visitors can experience the cockpit of an actual airplane. A photo zone is also available where visitors can take pictures wearing various professional uniforms, such as those of pilots, mechanics, and flight attendants.

2nd Floor: Space Hall

Along with exhibits related to space exploration, this section features galaxy-themed ceiling decorations, a 4D theater, a diorama zone, and models of future space and aviation cities. Visitors can also experience models that move when a button is pressed.

Experience Zone

There is a wealth of hands-on activities available, including making and flying paper airplanes, VR (Virtual Reality) simulators, and airplane escape slides.

In the 4D theater, special effects that stimulate the five senses—such as vibrations, wind, and scents—are added to the video, allowing visitors to indirectly experience actual flight or space exploration.

A T-50 Black Eagles flight simulation is also available.

Energy & Environment Experience

There is an energy experience zone where visitors can try powering an airplane using renewable energy, making it an excellent place to cultivate scientific thinking skills. The facility has been completely renovated, offering a pleasant interior, and various experiences and explanations tailored to children's perspectives are available.

Conveniences such as elevators, nursing rooms, diaper changing stations, stroller rentals, and parking are provided for a convenient visit.

Please note that exhibition and experience operating hours vary, and some programs, such as VR and 4D, require on-site registration or separate paid access. It is recommended to check the schedule and capacity limits in advance before visiting.

Located near the Sacheon Aerospace Museum, a combined admission ticket is available, allowing for a more enriching visit.

At the Aviation Industry Experience Hall on the first floor, visitors can wear costumes representing aviation professions (pilot, flight attendant, mechanic) and take photos at the photo zone.

Paper airplane flying and airplane assembly kit making experiences are available (4,000 KRW).

The 4D Theater is open to elementary school students and older, with a runtime of 17 minutes. Seats are available on a first-come, first-served basis with a total of 50 seats, so it is advisable to check in advance.

VR experiences include Paragliding Virtual Flight VR, Fighter Pilot VR, and Super Wings VR. On the second floor, you can enjoy free VR experiences and flight path simulations using air tubes.

At the space station, you can try on spacesuits, and coloring activities are also provided.

수소안전뮤지엄은 충청북도 음성군 맹동면 연미로 360-33에 위치해 있으.en:
The Hydrogen Safety Museum is located at 360-33, Yeonmi-ro, Maengdong-myeon, Eumseong-gun, Chungcheongbuk-do, and is an experience and education-focused exhibition hall operated by the Korea Gas Safety Corporation.

This museum provides information on gas and hydrogen safety in an easy and fun way. In particular, it offers various programs and exhibits designed to allow children to naturally broaden their understanding of future energy through hands-on experiences.

The first floor houses the lobby, information desk, lounge, and experience education rooms, while the second floor is equipped with spaces for full-scale experiences and education.

Gas Safety Experience Hall

Visitors can learn essential safety information for daily life, such as gas safety classes, basic gas knowledge, and emergency procedures for gas leaks, through intuitive graphics and interactive content.

In areas like 'Gas Safety Reminder' and the 'Gas Safety Chamber,' visitors can also participate in hands-on experiences where they can identify actual hazards and learn accident prevention methods.

Visitors can learn essential safety information for daily life, such as gas safety classes, basic gas knowledge, and emergency procedures for gas leaks, through intuitive graphics and interactive content. In areas such as 'Gas Safety Reminder' and 'Gas Safety Chamber,' visitors can participate in hands-on experiences where they can identify actual hazards and learn accident prevention methods.

Hydrogen Safety Promotion Hall

Visitors can engage with the eco-friendliness, safety, and potential of hydrogen as a future energy source through videos, exhibits, and various models organized by theme.

The hall is designed to allow visitors to directly examine and indirectly experience safety devices applied in real life, such as the safety of hydrogen storage containers and safety technologies used in charging stations.

Visitors can envision the future hydrogen society of 2050 and gain information on the significance of the hydrogen economy, international trends, and overcoming climate change.

Visitors can engage with the eco-friendliness, safety, and potential of hydrogen as a future energy source through videos, exhibits, and various models organized by theme.

The hall is designed to allow visitors to directly examine and indirectly experience safety devices applied in real life, such as the safety of hydrogen storage containers and safety technologies used in charging stations.

Visitors can envision the future hydrogen society of 2050 and gain information on the significance of the hydrogen economy, international trends, and overcoming climate change. 4D Theater

It is particularly popular among children and teenagers as they can experience global climate change, future energy societies, and cities utilizing hydrogen through vivid 4D videos.

The Hydrogen Safety Museum consists of a Gas Safety Experience Hall, a Hydrogen Safety Promotion Hall, and a 4D Theater.

Through engaging programs, children can have fun while gaining an understanding of hydrogen.

Admission is free. The museum is closed every Monday and Sunday, as well as on January 1st and during the Lunar New Year and Chuseok holidays. It is open on public holidays.

Operating Hours: 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM (Break for lunch from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM)

You must enter at least 10 minutes before the start of the experience and confirm your attendance at the information desk.

You can watch videos about hydrogen in the waiting area.

A Hydrogen Science Room and a Hydrogen Playground have been newly established. Advance reservations are required for the Hydrogen Science Room, so please book it together when booking the docent tour. Exiting during the tour is not permitted, so we recommend using the restroom beforehand.

In the 4D theater, the seats shake violently with wind effects during the performance, so please raise your hand to let us know if you feel dizzy.

Registering for the docent program, which includes explanations from a guide, makes the experience easier to understand and allows you to enjoy the visit more fully.

You must make a reservation for the docent program in advance via the website.

On the day of your visit, the Hydrogen Safety Museum will check for changes in the number of visitors or details via phone, so please answer the call.

Family restrooms, a nursing room, stroller rentals, and lockers are located on the first floor.

There is a dedicated parking lot, and parking is free.

A photo zone is also set up in front of the exhibition hall, making it a great spot to take family photos.

Near the Hydrogen Safety Museum, there are attractions where you can experience history and nature, such as the Jincheon Seokjang-ri Ancient Iron Production Site, Bongam Holy Site, and Maengdong Holy Site, making it a great place to enjoy a diverse day trip.

It is a special venue for a fun and easy experience where you can learn about hydrogen, a somewhat unfamiliar future energy source, with your children. We recommend this to the whole family, as it fosters knowledge and attitudes toward safety as well as curiosity about the future society.

With interactive exhibits, 4D media, and information on an eco-friendly future society, it will be a beneficial and enjoyable time for both children and parents. Fee: Free

소마미술관은 서울특별시 송파구 위례성대로 51, 올림픽공원 내에 위치해.en:
The SOMA Museum of Art is located within Olympic Park at 51, Wiryeoseong-daero, Songpa-gu, Seoul.

It possesses a history of transforming the cultural heritage of the 1988 Seoul Olympics into art. Opened in 2004 as the Seoul Olympic Museum of Art, it is now widely known by the name "SOMA."

The museum complex features the main building (Gallery 1), Gallery 2 (expanded in 2018), and a world-class outdoor sculpture park.

The sculpture park, spanning a total of 692,367 square meters, displays 221 contemporary sculptures by 155 artists from 66 countries. Visitors can freely stroll with their children while appreciating the artworks.

Designed by renowned architect Cho Seong-ryong, the museum building offers a unique atmosphere depending on the time of day and weather, thanks to a structure that blends natural light with diverse materials.

With various spaces including indoor and outdoor exhibition halls, a video art hall, studios, education rooms, and seminar rooms, visitors can engage not only in art appreciation but also in art experiences and educational activities. The outdoor park, where nature and sculpture harmonize, features walking paths, corridors, and a water garden, allowing you to stroll and play freely with your children.

Luggage lockers are available at the entrance for the convenience of leaving your belongings while viewing the exhibits, and there is also a souvenir shop before the exit.

Gallery 1 Operating Hours: 10:00 ~ 19:00

Gallery 2 Operating Hours: 10:00 ~ 18:00

Closed every Monday

Docent Tours: Tuesday ~ Friday at 11:00, 14:00, and 16:00

Docent tours are not available on weekends, so it is recommended to bring earphones and use the **audio guide (3,000 KRW)**.

Parking is available at the Olympic Park parking lot, and the fee is 600 KRW per 10 minutes. Hall 1 Adults (Ages 19–64): 15,000 won

Different exhibitions are currently running depending on the period, so it is recommended to check the website before visiting.

The SOMA Museum of Art is located within Songpa Olympic Park, and it is a good place to visit along with the Hanseong Baekje Museum and the Sculpture Park.

케니 배런 트리오 내한공연.en: Kenny Barron Trio's concert in Korea

[공연소개]\n\n재즈 피아니스트 케니 배론은 서정성과 스윙, 그리고 정.en:
[Concert Introduction]

Jazz pianist Kenny Barron is a master of modern jazz piano who has embodied lyricism, swing, and a sophisticated sense of harmony in perfect balance. He established his musical presence early on through collaborations with giants at the center of jazz history, such as Dizzy Gillespie, Stan Getz, and Freddie Hubbard, and has since steadily developed his own unique musical world over decades across a wide range of forms, from trios and solos to large-scale ensembles. His performances are always grounded in restrained lyricism and deep swing, conveying the intellectual yet warm charm inherent in jazz.

This concert holds special significance as it marks the first performance in Korea by the trio featuring Kenny Barron, bassist Alexis Cuadrado, and drummer Jonathan Blake. Notably, April 30th, the date of the concert, is UNESCO-designated International Jazz Day, making this a special stage to celebrate this unique day with the 83-year-old living legend of jazz.

Alexis Cuadrado, a Barcelona native based in New York, is an unrivaled bassist who combines the passion of flamenco with the intellect of modern jazz. Based on solid classical technique, he has collaborated with world-renowned masters such as Angelique Chizzo and Mark Turner. Furthermore, as a composer and leader, he employs narrative and sophisticated playing, adding depth and dynamism to Kenny Barron's elegant pianism.

Joining him on drums is Jonathan Blake, one of the leading figures in the contemporary jazz scene. Blake is a drummer who possesses both a traditional swing sensibility and a modern interpretation of rhythm, earning high acclaim for his dynamic yet detailed playing. His drumming goes beyond simple rhythmic accompaniment, acting as an active dialogue between the piano and bass to elevate the tension and energy of the entire trio.

The Kenny Barron Trio created by these three will present a modern sound rooted in the classical piano trio format, while naturally blending the individual personalities and experiences of each musician. Intricately layered harmonies, interplay that utilizes space, and improvisation that captures momentary inspiration clearly reveal the most essential charms of trio jazz. In particular, Kenny Barron’s musical insights, accumulated over many years on stage, will shine even more deeply through the close synergy with the two musicians.

Holded to commemorate Jazz Day, this performance by the Kenny Barron Trio goes beyond a simple visiting concert; it will be a valuable opportunity to witness firsthand the highest level of perfection achievable by a contemporary jazz trio. Offering a simultaneous experience of jazz’s intellectual depth, human warmth, and the vivid energy unique to a live stage, this performance is expected to be a special moment that will remain in the memories of Korean jazz fans for a long time.

랄랄라, 아이와 엄마가 함께하는 음악회.en: Lalala, a concert for mothers and children

[공연소개]\n\n아이와 부모가 함께 클래식 음악을 편안하게 만나는 시간.en:
[Performance Introduction]

This is a time for children and parents to comfortably encounter classical music together.

The performance is structured to help children naturally understand classical music they are hearing for the first time through stories and commentary.

This concert, titled "Lalala! A Concert for Children and Moms," introduces piano classical works that children can easily enjoy.

We present classical music with familiar melodies, such as Beethoven's *Für Elise*, Mozart's *Variations on *Twinkle Twinkle Little Star*, and Debussy's *Gollywog's Cakewalk*.

Through Chopin's Waltzes and various pieces from Saint-Saëns' *Carnival of Animals*, you can also encounter the diverse animals and stories featured in the music.

This is a program designed for children to listen to classical music without pressure and to experience the atmosphere and stories of the music together.

[Performance Introduction]

Seoul and Sihyang go to a classical music concert with their mom. As soon as the first piece begins, the two friends are completely captivated by the wonderful melody! However, a major incident occurs when a sudden vortex blows away and vanishes the conductor's score. They discover that this is a plan by Mr. Crescendo, a villain who intends to monopolize all the music in the world... Burning with a sense of justice and full of courage, Seoul and Sihyang embark on their first adventure with trembling hearts to find the missing score.

Shall we set off on an exciting adventure traveling the world and encountering the music of great composers with the Seoul Philharmonic Orchestra?

[Concert Introduction]

Voices that become a poem meet the orchestra.

The 'Special Concert' featuring La Poème and the Chungnam Symphony Orchestra is a special stage encompassing various genres, including pop, Korean ballads, and musicals.

La Poème, the world's first crossover group to include a traditional countertenor, presents a stage akin to a poem to the audience through the resonance rooted in vocal music and emotional expressiveness.

In this performance, they showcase not only La Poème's signature songs but also new interpretations that transcend genre boundaries through rich melodies with the orchestra.

The grandeur of classical music, the familiarity of popular music, and La Poème's unique artistic sensibility blend together to offer the audience a special experience.

[공연소개]\n\n- 현대음악작곡가 최진석의 오케스트라 신작 <Four.en:
[Concert Introduction]

- Contemporary Composer Choi Jin-seok’s New Orchestral Work <Four Pieces for Orchestra>

- Contemporary composer Choi Jin-seok, 3rd Prize winner at the Basel Composition Competition, presents a new orchestral work composed of four movements themed around waves, darkness, light, and wind.

Contemporary composer Choi Jin-seok’s new orchestral work, <Four Pieces for Orchestra>, consists of four pieces (movements) themed around waves, darkness, light, and wind. Each movement musically explores the different energies and states inherent in nature, forming a continuous flow through contrasts of intensity and stillness, creation and destruction, and tension and relaxation. Throughout the work, the movements of nature are depicted by applying the structural principles of music that the composer considers most important. This work will have its premiere with the Hankyung arte Philharmonic Orchestra conducting Kim Yu-won.

[Synopsis]

“A Lullaby for Lost Youth” – Comfort Shared Between Schubert and 21st-Century Youth

Schubert, who sang of hope and despair from his sickbed in 1823. The wandering of the young miller he depicted reflects the anxiety and loneliness of us living in 2026. We encounter an ironic song cycle of youth where failure is okay and pain is beautiful.

Tenor Jin Sung-won, a professor at Gachon University who nurtures the next generation, possesses exceptional interpretive skills and a warm, beautiful voice. His voice unravels the human anguish and youthful imagery composed by Schubert with vocal depth!

Pianist Choi Eun-ju, with her seasoned and delicate touch. Her accompaniment embodies the essence of Schubert’s lieder through piano melodies, ranging from the whispers of the stream to the young man’s turbulent psychological shifts!

KBS’ rising talent, Announcer Kim Jin-woong. His trustworthy commentary serves as a bridge, lowering the threshold of the beautiful Miller’s Daughter with his captivating voice and delivery! “Every night when I go to bed, I hope I will not wake up again… Only works created by sorrow can bring people the greatest joy…”

(From a letter Schubert sent to his friend Kupelwieser in 1824)

We present to you the song cycle “The Fair Maid of the Miller,” a record of the ‘will to live’ that Schubert left us.

[공연소개]\n\nUNDERCITY의 Soft Opening을 함께 열었.en:
[Concert Introduction]

Jeremy Olander, who co-hosted the soft opening of UNDERCITY, returns to Seongsu after a year. This time, rather than a single set, he will fill the stage with "Open to Close – All Night Long Set" (6 hours), completing the flow from the beginning to the end of the night as a single narrative.

Since his debut through Eric Prydz's Pryda Friends, he has crossed between world-renowned labels such as Drumcode, Anjunadeep, and Diynamic, establishing himself as one of the most trusted producers in the melodic house and techno scenes. His most significant signature is his delicate sound design and set composition that simultaneously designs emotion and structure. Through his own label, Vivrant, founded in 2014, he has also established his identity as both an artist and a curator.

This performance is not merely a visit to Korea, but a Vivrant Showcase and a symbolic night that ushers in the era of his debut album, *When The Rain Falls*. Releasing on March 13, this album is his most personal and reflective work, capturing years of artistic evolution and changes in his life.

"When The Rain Falls" aims for electronic music meant to be "listened to," rather than functional tracks for clubs. Completed based on his own experiences and emotions, this album showcases the direction of sound that Jeremy Olander has newly defined.

The album's worldview, unfolding starting with the first single "Apollo," reveals his expanded musical spectrum through various collaborations, centered on cinematic sound and vivid emotional lines. It marks a turning point where he has evolved beyond traditional progressive house toward a more mature and narrative sound.

The "Open to Close Set" to be held at UNDERCITY is a moment where his career, the narrative of his albums, and Vivrant's philosophy come together as one. For fans who have grown alongside his music, this night will remain a special experience to be remembered for a long time.

[시놉시스]\n \n 1막 1장\n\n궁전 안. 오늘은 왕자의 20세 생.en:
[Synopsis]

Act 1, Scene 1

Inside the palace. Today is the Prince's 20th birthday. The Prince and his friends are happily dancing with the court maidens. Just then, the Queen appears to congratulate the Prince on coming of age and presents him with a sword as a gift. After everyone leaves, Prince Siegfried, left alone, feels an unknown force repeatedly leading him somewhere.

Act 1, Scene 2

Led by this unknown force, he arrives at a lakeside in the forest. There, the Prince discovers swans that transform into human forms. Prince Siegfried falls for Princess Odette, the most beautiful of them all. She laments their fate, explaining that they are cursed by a genius devil to transform into swans by day and humans by night, and tells him that to break the spell, they must receive the unchanging love of one person. The Prince makes a vow of love, promises to announce their marriage at the ball the following day, and they part ways.

Act 2, Scene 1

The palace ballroom. The Prince greets guests while waiting for Odette to arrive. The prince is urged to choose a bride from among the princesses invited from Poland, Russia, Spain, Hungary, and Naples, but he shows little interest. Just then, the Devil appears with his daughter, Odile. The prince rushes toward Odile, who resembles Odette. The Devil begins to test the prince's emotions. Captivated by the charm of the Black Swan, Odile, the prince announces his marriage to her. At this moment, darkness suddenly descends, and a vision of a despairing Odette appears. Only then does the prince realize he has been played by the whims of fate and rushes to Swan Lake.

Act 2, Scene 2

The lakeside. Odette delivers the sad news to the swans, stating that due to the prince's betrayal, she is condemned to live as a swan forever. The prince rushes to beg for forgiveness. However, the Devil continues to interfere in an attempt to separate him from Odette. The prince tries to fight against fate, but the Devil's power is formidable. Just then, the moment Odette tells the prince that she forgives him, a miracle occurs in which their love overcomes the Devil's evil power.
